clue.text: Battle for pay rise?

parts.note: a fight over earnings could jokingly be called a struggle about wages, while the phrase also simply means to fight

explanation.surface: A union contemplating a fight with the bosses over a salary increase.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase meaning 'to fight' is read literally as a conflict waged over wages, which is exactly what a battle for a pay rise is.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage in hostilities is the idiom's normal sense; the clue adds a punning sense of conflict about earnings.

clue.text: Most angry antelope chasing bee away

indicators.note: with the bee sent away, those letters are removed

parts.note: a wildebeest, or gnu, is an African antelope

explanation.surface: A furious antelope runs after an insect until it leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes BEE from WILDEBEEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious or out of control makes one wild; the superlative means the most furious.

clue.text: Nice chap, one the curate didn't encounter

definitions.meaning: a decent, reliable sort of person
in the old Punch cartoon a curate says his bad egg is good in parts, so a wholly sound egg is one he never met

explanation.surface: A nice man the clergyman never got to meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A decent, likable person is idiomatically called this; the curate's egg was only partly sound.

clue.text: Pull away with the others

parts.note: the rest means the remaining ones

explanation.surface: Someone leaves along with everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench or forcibly take something from someone's grasp is to pull it away.

clue.text: One caned for rude noise?

definitions.meaning: a blowing sound of derision made with the tongue and lips

explanation.surface: A schoolboy is beaten for blowing a vulgar sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The berry grows on canes, and blowing one is a derisive spluttering noise.

clue.text: Examination claimed to be in error

indicators.note: letters that are in error are wrongly placed, so the word before is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a test result was asserted mistakenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in error' rearranges CLAIMED.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's check-up of a patient's health is called by this noun, a type of examination.

clue.text: Forces doctor to struggle to get the picture

parts.note: an MO is a medical officer in the armed forces
to vie is to compete or contend

explanation.surface: A military medic is made to fight to see an X-ray image.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is informally called a picture, as in going to the pictures.

clue.text: Is exact in detailing changes to set dish

indicators.note: changes made to the letters rearrange them

explanation.surface: A fussy chef alters how a plate is presented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges TO SET DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being meticulous about small points is the idiom, from adding the tittle on each small letter i.

clue.text: General character that may be changing dangerously?

definitions.meaning: the world's weather patterns, now altering because of global warming

explanation.surface: An army officer's personality might be shifting in a worrying way.
explanation.definitionFit: It means the prevailing atmosphere or mood of a time, and also the weather patterns now warming alarmingly.

clue.text: Arsonist in boat

definitions.meaning: one who sets fires, humorously one who lights them
a flat-bottomed barge for carrying goods to and from ships

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a fire-starter and a flat-bottomed cargo barge used in harbours.

clue.text: England footballer may go round with pride

definitions.meaning: players in England's women's national football team are nicknamed after the lion on the badge
a female big cat lives in a group of lions, called a pride

explanation.surface: A national team player might do a lap of honour feeling proud.
explanation.definitionFit: The England women's team are nicknamed after female lions, and such animals roam in social groups called prides.

clue.text: Checking, having change of heart and banning

indicators.note: the heart is the central letter of the word for checking, and it is swapped for another letter

parts.note: to vet is to check, so checking is vetting

explanation.surface: An official is reviewing something, rethinks it, and forbids it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having change of heart' swaps the middle T of VETTING for an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Blocking or prohibiting a proposal is what exercising a veto does, so banning fits the present participle.

clue.text: Like a good candidate? Let a celeb get involved

indicators.note: letters that get involved become tangled together, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a party: a famous person would make a winning nominee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get involved' rearranges LET A CELEB.
explanation.definitionFit: A promising candidate is one voters could choose, someone fit to win an election.

clue.text: Like to feed toddler something for breakfast

indicators.note: something given to feed someone goes into them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tot is a small child
as means like, in the sense of in the same way

explanation.surface: A parent wants to give a small child something in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like a verb about fondness, but it is the comparison word; 'to feed' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Grilled slices of bread are a standard morning meal item, eaten with butter or jam.

clue.text: Article among garments, Roman ones

indicators.note: one piece placed among the letters of another sits inside it

parts.note: togs is informal for clothes
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item of clothing sits among other clothes, some of them from ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts A inside TOGS; 'ones' stands for garments, so the definition is 'Roman garments'.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of ancient Rome wore loose draped robes, the classic Roman outer garment.

clue.text: Thus, one in airport's what you seek here

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: one letter is placed in the middle of the airport name

parts.note: Luton is a London airport, with the possessive S kept
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller stuck in a terminal looks for a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside LUTONS. LUTON is an airport north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvers seek the answers to the clues, here in the crossword itself.

clue.text: Person guilty of fraud as a tennis player?

definitions.meaning: a crook running a dishonest business scheme
humorously, one who wields a racket, like a tennis player

explanation.surface: A sports star is exposed as a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler who runs a dishonest racket is the normal sense; the second is a pun on a tennis racket.

clue.text: Secretly entitled to extravagant dance demo

indicators.note: something extravagant goes wildly beyond the normal, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A lavish performance showcase is given a secret title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extravagant' rearranges DANCE DEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Given a covert alias for secrecy means being called by an assumed title.

clue.text: Showed detectives acted

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
to play a part is to act

explanation.surface: Police officers put on a performance for an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit or put something on view is to show it, past tense in both.

clue.text: Son admitted to proper nationality

indicators.note: a letter admitted to a word is let inside it

parts.note: decent means proper or respectable

explanation.surface: A boy is let into a respectable home of his ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted to' puts S inside DECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry or origin, as in being of Irish extraction, is a sense close to nationality.

clue.text: Largely counterfeit toiletry

parts.note: the hair wash's name is mostly made up of a word meaning fake, sham, which forms its first four letters

explanation.surface: A bottle of hair product that is mostly a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger calls this 'not the clearest clue': SHAM, meaning counterfeit, takes up most of the word, with POO left over unclued.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid soap for washing the hair is a common bathroom toiletry.

clue.text: Places to swim found returning to vessel

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: swimming pools

explanation.surface: Swimming spots are discovered on the way back to a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns POOLS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A small single-masted sailing boat is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Dismissed team not back in the pavilion?

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A cricket team has been bowled out but has not yet returned to the clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket pavilion is the clubhouse a dismissed batsman walks back to.
explanation.definitionFit: Not inside a building is being out of doors, here not yet back inside the cricket clubhouse.

clue.text: Flawless French oddly cheeky to conceal

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pert means saucy or cheeky

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters picks the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A French person is strangely impudent about hiding something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of French; 'to conceal' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any fault or defect is an exact synonym.

clue.text: Public transport's turnaround is quick and efficient

indicators.note: a turnaround is a reversal, so the word for the transport is read backwards

parts.note: trams are a form of public transport; the apostrophe-s goes with the following word as 'has', a link

explanation.surface: Praise for how fast a city's buses turn round at the terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnaround' reverses TRAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisk and capable, as in a sharp, well-run service, is a sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Maestro no longer seen on the buses

definitions.meaning: an orchestra's leader with a baton

definitions.text: no longer seen on the buses
definitions.meaning: the ticket collector on a British bus, a job largely abolished

explanation.surface: A famous musician has given up taking public transport.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both the one who directs an orchestra and the old ticket collector on buses.

clue.text: Cycle around a bit: it's cloudless

indicators.note: a bit of the words is taken, so the letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: Go for a short bike ride while the sky is clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' points to letters within cyCLE ARound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky with no cloud is a fine, bright one, so the adjective fits weather.

clue.text: Across the pond Sam is one of the family

definitions.text: Across the pond Sam is one of the family

parts.words: Across the pond Sam is one of the family
parts.note: in America, across the Atlantic, the national personification Sam has a family title as a relative

explanation.surface: An American called Sam is a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the pond' means in the USA, whose personification is Uncle Sam.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a family relative, and that title goes before Sam in the American figure.

clue.text: Carefully examine page in old learning

indicators.note: the page letter is placed in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former
lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: A scholar studies one leaf of an ancient body of knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old learning' reads as one phrase in the surface but splits into two pieces; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate or look into something thoroughly is to inspect it closely.

clue.text: Equipment to slice nice ham

indicators.note: slicing cuts something up, so these letters are chopped and rearranged

explanation.surface: A deli counter's slicer for cutting good gammon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to slice' rearranges NICE HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical device or apparatus counts as a piece of equipment.

clue.text: Appropriate clothing a little short

indicators.note: the clothing word is cut short by a single letter at its end

parts.note: trousers are an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A dress code note: shorts are fitting wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little short' drops the final S of TROUSERS. The verb is informal British for pocketing money.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket or take something, often money, for oneself is the informal verb; appropriate in its seize sense.

clue.text: At its most low, river a nuisance

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a pest is an annoying person or thing

explanation.surface: A troublesome river is at its lowest ebb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowest in position or depth is a superlative meaning furthest down.
